composition.story: Stacking needs base-model predictions on rows the model never trained on. Split 100 training rows into 5 folds. Each round trains the base model on four folds and predicts the fifth. Together, those held-out predictions form the out-of-fold column.

aha.observation: Each out-of-fold prediction comes from a base model that never saw that row. Five held-out slices together form the column the meta-model trains on.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons; keyboard arrow keys; names kept when disabled at ends

regions.label: Meta-model
phases: fit on OOF column and labels

states.label: Split
states.sentence: The 100 training rows are split into five folds of 20 rows each.
states.why: Every row belongs to exactly one fold, so each gets held out exactly once.

states.label: Round 1 fit
states.sentence: Round 1 holds out fold 1 and trains the base model on folds 2–5.
states.why: Held-out rows must stay out of training, or predictions on them would be optimistic.

states.label: Round 1 predict
states.sentence: The model predicts fold 1, which it never saw. Those 20 predictions fill the first slots.
states.why: This is the first slice of honest, out-of-sample predictions.

states.label: Round 2
states.sentence: Round 2 holds out fold 2, trains a fresh base model on folds 1, 3, 4, 5, and predicts fold 2.
states.why: A new fit each round keeps the held-out fold unseen by the model that predicts it.

states.label: Rounds 3–4
states.sentence: Rounds 3 and 4 repeat the same procedure, holding out folds 3 and 4 in turn.
states.why: Each round adds 20 new out-of-fold predictions without overwriting earlier ones.

states.label: Round 5
states.sentence: Round 5 holds out fold 5 and fills the last 20 slots. All 100 rows now have a prediction.
states.why: Five rounds times 20 held-out rows covers every training row exactly once.

states.label: Meta-model fit
states.sentence: The completed column becomes the meta-model's input. Each value came from a model that never saw that row.
states.why: Honest inputs let the meta-model learn how far to trust the base model.

readouts.label: Rows predicted by a model that saw them

1.reason: The fixed picture of five folds, the base model, the OOF column and the meta-model, with train and predict links, answers how every row gets an out-of-sample prediction.

2.reason: The aha state s7 is the final step of a user-driven stepper, and it shows the full OOF column feeding the meta-model with 0 rows predicted by a model that saw them.

3.reason: The single Step control changes the active regions and readouts in every state, so it is the experiment parameter and the outcomes differ from step to step.

4.reason: Most parts trace to declared state, but s4 and s6 list the held-out fold and the oof region as active alongside the training folds, and s2 omits the held-out fold 1 from active, so the highlights do not cleanly match the roles named in the sentences.

6.reason: Story, step labels, callout targets and readouts all refer to the same folds, rounds, base model, OOF column and meta-model.

7.reason: Seven states, each with a callout, ghost and three readouts over eight regions, plus the s5 grouping of two rounds in one state, go beyond what a detailed scene needs.

8.reason: The numbers check out: 4 × 20 = 80 rows per fit, 20 slots added per round, running totals of 20, 40, 80 and 100, and 5 × 80 base fits in total.
